extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom/style-guide resource for journalists and media professionals to help them cover diverse communities with accurate, authoritative and sensitive language. It specifies scope, sourcing, editorial practices, and conventions for presenting and attributing terms and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, authority and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversity Style Guide is a resource to help journalists and other media professionals cover a complex, multicultural world with accuracy, authority and sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language and terms that reflect factual correctness, demonstrate subject-matter knowledge, and show cultural sensitivity when writing about people and communities different from yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of topics covered
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide includes terms and phrases related to race/ethnicity; religion; sexual orientation; gender identity; age and generation; drugs and alcohol; and physical, mental and cognitive disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consulting the guide, focus on these explicitly listed topic areas as the primary domains for recommended terminology and usage guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and preference for established external style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the terms were taken directly from style guides prepared by other organizations. In those cases the terms link back to the original guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer language and definitions from authoritative organizations (e.g., AAJA, GLAAD, NABJ, NLGJA, National Center on Disability and Journalism, Religion News Association, etc.). Adopt their recommended usage unless there is a clearly documented reason to adapt it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citation for each term
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of each term is noted at the end of each entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparency by indicating the origin of definitions and linking back to original source material when applicable; note when terms were adapted or newly written by the guide's editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bracketed clarifications for added information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information included in brackets [ ] was added to the original definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bracketed text to signal editorial additions or clarifications to sourced definitions so readers can distinguish original wording from editor-added context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with experts and field leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: This guide takes wisdom and advice from leaders in the field who have researched and considered the cultural, political and linguistic meanings of words. No one person can determine the correct usage of a word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on research, consultation, and consensus among subject-matter experts rather than individual intuition; weigh cultural, political and linguistic meanings before prescribing usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial authorship and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversity Style Guide was edited by Rachele Kanigel... It was reviewed by April Bethea, chair of the SPJ Diversity Committee. Research assistants and numerous contributors helped assemble and edit definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document editorial responsibility and peer review; indicate contributors and reviewers to show the guide's credibility and the collaborative process behind entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: guidance, context and nuance (not policing 'political correctness')
rubrics_metrics.description: In recent years there’s been much talk about 'political correctness.' This is not a guide to being politically correct. Rather, it offers guidance, context and nuance for media professionals struggling to write about people who are different from themselves and communities different from their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to educate and provide contextualized guidance for careful reporting rather than prescribing a rigid list of 'correct' words; prioritize understanding and nuance in application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended practical use in classrooms and newsrooms
rubrics_metrics.description: The companion book and the guide are widely used in classrooms, newsrooms and media organizations around North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design entries and examples to be usable for both teaching and day-to-day newsroom practice; make guidance accessible for journalists at different experience levels.
